clue.text: As worn by fatherless seven-year-old Sigmund?

definitions.text: As worn by fatherless seven-year-old Sigmund?

parts.note: surface reading: a petticoat or undergarment that a little boy has on
setter's reading: the young psychoanalyst wishing his father gone, the Oedipal wish that leaks out in an unguarded remark

explanation.surface: A dressing-up question about what young Sigmund wore as a fatherless boy.
explanation.walkthrough: A slip is both an undergarment and a revealing error; the 'fatherless' child nods to Freud's Oedipus complex, the wish such errors are said to betray.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a verbal error believed to reveal a hidden wish, named after the founder of psychoanalysis.

clue.text: Maximum/minimum comfort? Neither is complete support

indicators.note: neither word is complete, so each one loses its final letter

parts.note: at maximum capacity is full
the least possible comfort is a crumb of comfort

explanation.surface: A question about how much comfort a support gives, maximum or minimum.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words are cut short: FULL loses its last L and CRUMB its last B, giving FUL + CRUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A fulcrum is the pivot point on which a lever rests and turns, a physical prop.

clue.text: In the beginnings of each year, the Royal Family is timeless, but it is not tideless

indicators.note: the royal house sits in between the two opening letters
beginnings asks for the opening letter of each word that follows

parts.note: first letters of each and year

indicators.note: less time means a single T, the abbreviation for time, is dropped

parts.note: the Stuarts were a royal dynasty of Scotland and England

explanation.surface: A year-opening remark that the royals are timeless though their realm is tidal.
explanation.walkthrough: The Stuarts were the royal house of Scotland and later England. The definition is cryptic: a river mouth is exactly where the tide does reach.
explanation.definitionFit: An estuary is the tidal mouth of a river, where sea water flows in and out daily.

clue.text: Sly trader could be involved in dye trade

definitions.note: describes the person rather than naming him

indicators.note: could be invites the solver to see what else those letters might become when rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A cunning merchant suspected of a part in the dyeing business.
explanation.definitionFit: A drysalter was a dealer in dyes, gums, salted meats and chemical dry goods, an old trade name.

clue.text: Marketplace has gone with the sun

parts.note: gone by, in the past: ago
Ra is the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: A market square that has disappeared with the sunset.
explanation.definitionFit: An agora was the open public square of an ancient Greek city, used for trade and assembly.

clue.text: Bribe the Queen''s Singers

parts.note: a sop is something given to pacify or buy off
a rani is an Indian queen

explanation.surface: Someone bribing the monarch's choir.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is', joining wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Soprani is the Italian plural of soprano, the highest female or boy voices in a choir.

clue.text: Back Joe to smuggle old instrument in ? he''s cool

indicators.note: back means the whole result is read from end to start
to smuggle is to carry something hidden inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: GI Joe is a nickname for an American soldier
a rebec is a medieval bowed instrument

explanation.surface: Backing a calm smuggler who sneaks an antique instrument across a border.
explanation.definitionFit: An iceberg is figuratively a cold, unemotional person who shows no warmth.

clue.text: Recurring pain may be what''s taken away poet?

parts.note: a Chinese is a British name for a takeaway meal from a Chinese restaurant
Robert Burns, Scotland's national poet

explanation.surface: A query whether a poet having been taken away causes ongoing pain.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'a Chinese' is everyday shorthand for a Chinese takeaway meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinese burns are a playground torment of twisting the skin of a forearm, often inflicted again and again.

clue.text: Servants all losing head on line

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter of the phrase is dropped

parts.note: all of it is the lot
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: Domestic staff all being decapitated on the line.
explanation.definitionFit: Helotry means the body of helots, the serfs of ancient Sparta, so a collective term for bondsmen.

clue.text: Overwhelm with inverted ironwork?

indicators.note: inverted tells you to turn round the order of the two halves of the compound word

parts.note: the second half, work, is op, short for opus
the first half, iron, is press, as with clothes

explanation.surface: Crushing someone with ornamental metalwork turned upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ironwork' looks like one thing, but split it into its two halves and turn their order round. OP is short for opus.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppress is to weigh down or crush people by harsh force, close in sense to overwhelm.

clue.text: Big hoax involving Don with outward appearance of windmills?

definitions.text: Big hoax involving Don with outward appearance of windmills?

indicators.note: involving suggests things tangled together, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: letters to be mixed
taken as written

indicators.note: outward appearance means only the outside, the first and last letters

parts.note: outer letters of windmills

explanation.surface: Don Quixote's great delusion of fighting windmills, thought giants.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: Don Quixote tilting at windmills is fighting an imaginary foe.
explanation.definitionFit: Shadow boxing is sparring against an imaginary opponent, just as Quixote charged windmills he imagined were giants.

clue.text: Joy-riding, initially in a van that's out of control

indicators.note: out of control means the letters career about into a new order
initially points to the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: first letter of riding
taken as written

explanation.surface: Joyriders tearing about in a stolen van that has gone out of control.
explanation.definitionFit: Nirvana is a state of perfect bliss, a Buddhist ideal used loosely for supreme happiness.

clue.text: Walk for a disabled lawyer

parts.note: taken as written
lame means disabled in the leg
DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecutor

explanation.surface: A walking route provided for a lawyer with a disability.
explanation.definitionFit: An alameda is a tree-lined public promenade, a Spanish word for a shaded walkway.

clue.text: Monotonous setter boarding express

indicators.note: boarding means getting on and inside a vehicle, so one piece goes in the other

parts.note: to express is to say
the setter refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: A dull puzzle-setter climbing onto an express train.
explanation.definitionFit: Samey is informal British for tediously alike, lacking variety, hence dull and repetitive.

clue.text: Addressing a reproof

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a scolding, as one noun

explanation.definitionFit: Read as a verb phrase it means speaking to someone; as a hyphenated noun it means a telling-off.

clue.text: He may help you gain access to hair fashion

definitions.text: He may help you gain access

parts.note: a lock is a tress of hair
to smith is to fashion or forge metal

explanation.surface: A hairdresser helping clients get into the latest styles.
explanation.definitionFit: A locksmith makes and opens locks, so is called on when someone is locked out.

clue.text: Curiosities of old trains: independent end-to-end carriages

indicators.note: end-to-end suggests the second carriage is turned round, its end first

parts.note: BR, British Rail, the former national railway
I is the abbreviation for independent
a cab and a car, two kinds of carriage

explanation.surface: Collectible relics of the old railway, with carriages coupled together.
explanation.walkthrough: BR is British Rail, the old nationalised railway. Only the second carriage is turned end to end; the first stays as it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Bric-a-brac is miscellaneous small ornaments and curios of little value, odds and ends.

clue.text: One confused and in a state

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: confused means the following words are muddled into a new order

parts.note: letters to be mixed

explanation.surface: Someone muddled and in a right state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a state' looks like an idiom for being upset, but 'state' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is one of the fifty United States, in the American Midwest.

clue.text: Unlimited alcohol consumed in a limited time factor

indicators.note: something consumed goes inside, so one piece sits within the other
without limits means the word loses its two ends

parts.note: taken as written
L standing for limited, as in Ltd cut down
liquor is alcoholic drink
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Drinking without restraint during a short time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unlimited' strips both ends off the drink. An aliquot part is a mathematician's term, so 'factor' is a fair definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An aliquot is a number that divides another exactly with no remainder, an exact divisor.

clue.text: Abandon the B-team

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to cancel or call off
second meaning: in American sport, the second-string players

explanation.walkthrough: In US school and college sport the reserve players are called the scrubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally the verb means cancel a plan, and the noun names reserve or second-rate players.

clue.text: Loose nurse harbours need

definitions.note: verb: to loosen or let go

indicators.note: to harbour is to shelter within, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: SEN is a State Enrolled Nurse, a former British grade
a need is a lack

explanation.surface: A nurse quietly keeping a need hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: To slacken is to loosen or relax a rope or grip, as the verb loose means.

clue.text: Some extra for women in tatters — detailed here

definitions.text: Some extra for women in tatters — detailed here

parts.words: Some extra for women in tatters
parts.note: surface reading: a walk-on actress in ragged costume
setter's reading: the spare body part taken from Adam to make Eve, and the tatters are ribbons with the tail cut

explanation.surface: A film extra playing a ragged woman, described in detail.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis woman was made from Adam's rib. Tatters are ribbons; 'detailed' clips its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A rib is one of the curved bones of the chest, and Genesis says Eve was formed from one.

clue.text: Bloody attractive woman there, just on the left!

parts.note: a red is a left-winger
a dish is slang for an attractive person

explanation.surface: An exclamation at a gorgeous woman standing just to the left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the left' places the political colour in front of the attractive woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bloody is stained with blood and so tinged with a red colour.

clue.text: A snail left one in a spell

indicators.note: in places these letters within the word that follows

parts.note: a hex is a spell or curse
L for left
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A snail abandoned somebody under an enchantment.
explanation.definitionFit: Helix is the genus of land snails that includes the common garden snail.

clue.text: Here tub-thumper stands to flatter and fight

parts.note: to soap is to flatter, as in soft soap
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: A ranting orator who stands to flatter or pick a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: A tub-thumper is a ranting public speaker, a Speakers' Corner orator.
explanation.definitionFit: A soapbox is an improvised platform, once a crate, for street-corner speeches.

clue.text: Sleds reversing over a lake bird

indicators.note: reversing means the word runs backwards
over here means placed across and around, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: luges are small racing toboggans
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Sleds sliding backwards across a frozen lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A seagull is a common coastal bird of the gull family.

clue.text: Obscure tavern in which king meets low woman, it is rumoured

indicators.note: in which means the following pieces sit inside the place named

parts.note: an inn is a tavern
K for king in chess

indicators.note: something rumoured is heard by word of mouth, so go by sound

parts.note: a disreputable woman, spelt to match the sound

explanation.surface: A disreputable pub where a king rendezvous with a woman of ill repute, so gossip says.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it describes pedantic, learned vocabulary that is hard for ordinary readers to grasp.

clue.text: Spooner''s preferred form of transaction?

parts.note: surface reading: a way of buying something, trading in an old item
setter's reading: Spooner famously swapped bits of words, a trade of word pieces

explanation.surface: A query about which kind of deal the Reverend Spooner liked best.
explanation.walkthrough: The Reverend Spooner gave his name to swapping the opening sounds of words, exchanging their parts.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a deal where an old item is handed over as partial payment toward a new one.
